'''Olav Vadstein''' (born 14 February 1955){{Citation needed|date=February 2010}} is a [[Norwegian people|Norwegian]] [[professor]] of [[Microbial ecology|Microbial Ecology]] at the [[Norwegian University of Science and Technology]].<ref name=cv>{{cite web|url=http://www.ntnu.no/employees/olav.vadstein|title=Olav Vadstein|publisher=Norwegian University of Science and Technology}}</ref>

According to his [[web page]], Vadstein is interested in [[aquatic ecosystem]]s

"both natural and unnatural ([[human]] created). Besides basic aspects, I’m interested in applied microbial ecology, which can be placed under the heading [[Environmental biotechnology|Environmental Biotechnology]]."

His most highly cited papers are:
*J. Skjermo, O. Vadstein, Techniques for [[microbe|microbial]] control in the intensive rearing of marine [[larva]]e in ''Aquaculture,'' 77, Issues 1–4, 1 July 1999, Pages 333-343- cited 378 times according to [[Google Scholar]]<ref name="GS">[https://scholar.google.com/scholar?hl=en&as_sdt=0%2C33&q=Olav+Vadstein&btnG=] Google Scholar web page</ref>
*Vadstein O. (2000) [[Heterotrophic]], [[Plankton]]ic [[Bacteria]] and [[Phosphorus cycle|Cycling of Phosphorus]]. In: Schink B. (eds) ''Advances in Microbial Ecology'' vol 16. Springer, Boston, MA- cited 184 times<ref name=GS />
*Vadstein, O. The use of [[immunostimulation]] in marine larviculture: possibilities and challenges. ''Aquaculture'' Volume 155, Issues 1–4, 20 September 1997, Pages 401–417 Cited 179 times<ref name=GS />
